A little about my own experiences. . .

      For those who have not yet cut out most refined/added sugar from your diet, I highly recommend that you try! Any substance can be addictive, but sugar is going to have a tighter grasp on you. Evolutionarily, we always sought out high calorie foods in order to survive. That was alright because we probably had to do a lot of physical labor in general and to obtain said food.

      In the modern era, we are much more sedentary and barely need to expend any energy to get our hands on high-calories foods. The food industry exploits this evolutionary traits and contributes to derailing our health. Ultimately, however, the foods you eat are a choice. Educate yourself and others, and watch out for your sugar intake. This will include simple and refined carbohydrates from other sources, like white rice, corn-based products, white bread, etc.

      I used to drink a lot of soda, juice, and sweetened tea. I used to do FOUR (FOUR) loaded spoons of sugar in a cup of tea -- anything less and I couldn't "taste* it. Damn, my parents would yell at me so much over that, and I was just annoyed by it (I do 1-1.5 these days).
I used to eat a lot of candy, ice cream, and baked goods. Fruit would taste nice, but not as nice as a pack of skittles. My cravings would be urgent, constant, and emotional (now my cravings are more dependent on my hormonal cycle than anything else, ha). It was basically slavery.

      Nowadays, pretty much all candy disgusts me. Outside of the occasional decent/higher quality chocolate, I don't do candy (and I'm tellin' ya. . . I did a lot of it). I am never tempted by the bakery section and rarely by the soda section (must be some lingering effects of caffeine. Plus, I always loved that fun fizz!) Out of habit, I still serve myself a lot of ice cream, but I find myself finishing only a third or half because I'm fed up with the sugar. I'm sure that not buying these products ultimately saves money in the long-run, because they are deliberately less satisfying so that we must buy more of it. And now fruit tastes amazing! In fact, fruit almost feels like cheating.

      I'm not saying, don't eat refined sugar, ever. But it would be good to make a clean cut initially. Once you get to the point where seeing it around doesn't trigger a craving and where you are relishing fruits, maybe have the occasional soda or whatever. It may take months, but I guarantee it will be worth it. I feel so refreshed without that stuff in my life. The max recommended amount of added sugar is 4-5 tsp for women and 5-6 for men each day, but I think I only sometimes pass two. We do a lot of home-cooked meals in my household, too, and that does help.
For those who have successfully managed to do so, how do you feel having removed most refined sugar from your diet? (I feel like an emacipated slave!) What was your process to get there?
